propositions: When multiple git bundle objects exist for a single S3 ref, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed'; git-remote-s3's push helper rejects all writes while bundles > 1, causing retries to stall at unresolvable ambiguity.

Upstream's git-s3 doctor is non-functional for autonomous fleets: it blocks on interactive input() prompts (crashing on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's events instead of merging them, causing permanent data loss from the append-only event log.

The S3 multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at the bundle layer; it is healable by acquiring the helper's per-ref lock, fetching all divergent bundle heads locally, losslessly merging them via iterated 2-parent merges (following sync's existing _union_merge semantics), writing the merged tip as a new bundle durably before deleting originals, and retrying the push.

The heal must write the merged bundle before deleting any original bundle and never delete the merged tip, guaranteeing that at least one bundle carrying full merged history remains remotely at every crash point, so mid-delete crashes leave the state re-healable to a single lossless bundle on the next run.

Concurrent heal attempts must serialize via the helper's own acquire_lock/release_lock (conditional-put, 60s TTL, stale-lock steal); if a doctor loses the lock, it backs off and the next push retry accepts the winner's collapsed remote, avoiding heal thrash.

The doctor reuses rebar's existing merge logic (sync._union_merge with 2-parent merges, --allow-unrelated-histories for unmerged heads, merge=ours for .bridge_state/*), commits no events under genuine conflicts (aborts, deletes nothing remotely, surfaces fsck-recover), and adds no direct boto3 dependency to core rebar (boto3 ships transitively with git-remote-s3 under the [s3] extra).
